title: 复杂度到底怎么量 — 纯随机和纯有序，都不复杂 · 复杂性科学 T41
title_en: Measuring complexity — neither pure order nor pure randomness · Complexity Science T41

questions.question: 香农熵和柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度作为「复杂度」的尺子，在同一个地方翻了车。是哪里？
options: 它们都把满分发给完全有序的东西，比如一页全是字母 A
它们都只能用于通信工程，无法用于生物或社会系统
它们都无法区分看起来随机和真的随机，比如圆周率的小数位
它们都把满分发给完全随机的东西，比如一串抛硬币的结果
questions.explanation: 熵的排序是乱码 > 有意义文本 > 纯重复；真正随机的串没有比照抄更短的描述，柯氏复杂度也最高。可我们想说的「复杂」应在两端都低分。柯氏复杂度恰恰修好了「看起来随机 vs 真的随机」——圆周率几行程序就能生成。
questions.question_en: Shannon entropy and Kolmogorov complexity, used as measures of complexity, fail in the same place. Where?
options_en: Both give the top score to things that are perfectly ordered, such as a page of nothing but A
Both apply only to communications engineering, not to biological or social systems
Both fail to distinguish what looks random from what is random, such as the digits of π
Both give the top score to things that are purely random, such as a string of coin flips
questions.explanation_en: Entropy ranks gibberish above prose above repetition, and a truly random string has no description shorter than itself, so its Kolmogorov complexity is maximal too — yet what we mean by complex should score low at both ends. Kolmogorov complexity actually does separate 'looks random' from 'is random': π's digits come from a few lines of code.

questions.question: 同事抱怨一份日志「复杂得看不懂」。你用 gzip 一压，它只剩原来的 5%；换一份压不动的。这两个结果分别能说明什么？
options: 压得动说明它很复杂，因为里面信息量大；压不动说明它简单
压不动就证明它确实复杂，应当投入更多人手去处理
压得动说明复杂只是重复；压不动只说明还没证明它简单
两种结果都证明不了什么，压缩率和复杂度毫无关系
questions.explanation: 压缩率是柯氏复杂度的上界：压得动就证明存在更短的描述，「复杂」是重复，该去重而不是加人。但柯氏复杂度不可计算，压不动只代表你还没找到更短的描述，这个检验只在一个方向有效。
questions.question_en: A colleague complains a log file is 'too complex to follow'. You gzip it and it shrinks to 5% of its size; another file won't compress. What do these two results tell you?
options_en: The first is highly complex because it holds lots of information; the second is simple
The second proves it really is complex and deserves more people working on it
The first is mostly repetition; the second only shows you haven't yet proven it simple
Neither proves anything, since compression has nothing to do with complexity
questions.explanation_en: Compression gives an upper bound on Kolmogorov complexity: if it compresses, a shorter description exists and the 'complexity' is repetition — dedupe it rather than add staff. But Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable, so failure to compress only means you haven't found a shorter description; the test works in one direction only.

questions.question: 一套跑了十年的祖传流程，其中几十条规则都能对上一次具体事故。按「逻辑深度」的视角，推倒重写它的真实成本主要是什么？
options: 重新踩一遍那些坑、换回积累的反馈所需的时间
几乎为零，因为规则的最短描述并不长
把规则重新写成代码的时间，规则写得越短就越便宜
取决于文档有多长，文档越长重建越难
questions.explanation: 逻辑深度问的是从最短描述跑出这个东西要多少步：描述可以很短，但里面压着一段无法回放的计算，只能重跑一遍。说不出几条规则来历的流程才是浅的，重写成本约等于写代码的时间；它的价值与篇幅大小无关。
questions.question_en: A decade-old legacy process has dozens of rules, each traceable to a specific incident. From the perspective of logical depth, what is the real cost of rewriting it from scratch?
options_en: The time to step on all those landmines again and regain that accumulated feedback, often an order of magnitude more
Nearly nothing, since the shortest description of the rules isn't long
The time to re-code the rules, which is cheap if they are short
It depends on how long the documentation is; the longer it is, the harder to rebuild
questions.explanation_en: Logical depth asks how many steps it takes to run from the shortest description to the object: the description can be short while the object embodies computation that can't be replayed, only rerun. A process whose rules have no traceable origins is shallow, and rewriting costs little more than coding; depth has nothing to do with size.
